entries.title: Mark 1:1
segments: Beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;

entries.title: Mark 1:2
segments: even as it is written in the prophet Isaiah,/@Behold, I am sending my messenger before your face to prepare your way.

entries.title: Mark 1:3
segments: The voice of one crying aloud: In the desert make ready a road for the Lord. Make his paths straight/@.

entries.title: Mark 1:4
segments: In the desert came John who baptized, and preached a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins;

entries.title: Mark 1:5
segments: and all the land of Judea, and all the people of Jerusalem, kept going out to him, and were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.

entries.title: Mark 1:6
segments: And John was clothed with camel's hair, and he had a leather girdle round his loins, and he ate locusts, and "honey of the wood."

entries.title: Mark 1:7
segments: He made proclamation: "There is One mightier than I coming after me, and I am not worthy to stoop down and unfasten his sandal strap;

entries.title: Mark 1:8
segments: I have baptized you in water, but he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit."

entries.title: Mark 1:9
segments: It was at that time that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan;

entries.title: Mark 1:10
segments: and as soon as he rose from the water he saw the sky cleft asunder, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him,

entries.title: Mark 1:11
segments: and a voice from the sky: "Thou art my Son, my beloved; in thee is my delight."

entries.title: Mark 1:12
segments: Then the Spirit drove him at once into the desert,

entries.title: Mark 1:13
segments: and he remained in the desert for forty days, tempted by Satan; and he was among the wild beasts, but the angels were ministering to him.

entries.title: Mark 1:14
segments: After John had been thrown into prison Jesus came into Galilee preaching the gospel of God.

entries.title: Mark 1:15
segments: "The time is now come," he said, "and the kingdom of God is near! Repent and believe the gospel."

entries.title: Mark 1:16
segments: And as he was passing along by the sea of Galilee he saw Simon and Andrew, Simon's brother, casting their net into the sea, for they were fishermen;

entries.title: Mark 1:17
segments: so Jesus said to them, "Come after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men."

entries.title: Mark 1:18
segments: At once they left their nets and followed him.

entries.title: Mark 1:19
segments: As he went a little farther on he saw James, the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in their boat mending the nets.

entries.title: Mark 1:20
segments: Straightway he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants and went after him.

entries.title: Mark 1:21
segments: So they came to Capernaum, and as soon as the Sabbath Day came he went into the synagogue and began to teach.

entries.title: Mark 1:22
segments: They were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them with authority, not like the Scribes.

entries.title: Mark 1:23
segments: And at that very moment, there in their synagogue, a man in the grip of an unclean spirit shrieked out:

entries.title: Mark 1:24
segments: "What business have you with us, you Jesus of Nazareth? Are you come to destroy us? I know you who you are, the Holy One of God."

entries.title: Mark 1:25
segments: But Jesus rebuked him, saying: "Be quiet! Come out of him."

entries.title: Mark 1:26
segments: So the unclean spirit, after tearing him, came out of him with a loud cry;

entries.title: Mark 1:27
segments: and every one was amazed so that they began questioning among themselves: "What does this mean? A new teaching with authority? He lays commands even upon unclean spirits and they obey him."

entries.title: Mark 1:28
segments: And at once his fame spread everywhere through that part of Galilee.

entries.title: Mark 1:29
segments: On leaving the synagogue they went at once with James and John to the house of Simon and Andrew.

entries.title: Mark 1:30
segments: Now Simon's mother-in-law lay sick of fever, and without delay they told him about her.

entries.title: Mark 1:31
segments: So he came and took her hand and raised her up. The fever left her at once, and she began to wait upon them.

entries.title: Mark 1:32
segments: At evening when the sun had set, people came and brought to him all the sick and demon-possessed,

entries.title: Mark 1:33
segments: and the whole town was gathered at the door.

entries.title: Mark 1:34
segments: He cured many who were ill with various diseases, and drove out many demons. But he did not allow the demons to speak, because they knew who he was.

entries.title: Mark 1:35
segments: In the morning he rose a great while before day and went out to a desert place, and there prayed.

entries.title: Mark 1:36
segments: And Simon and his companions hunted him up,

entries.title: Mark 1:37
segments: and told him, "Every one is looking for you."

entries.title: Mark 1:38
segments: "Let us go away," he answered, "to the neighboring country towns, that I may preach there, too; because for that purpose I came forth."

entries.title: Mark 1:39
segments: So he went throughout Galilee, preaching in the synagogues and driving out demons.

entries.title: Mark 1:40
segments: One day a leper cane to him and besought him as he knelt down to him, saying, "If you choose, you are able to cleanse me."

entries.title: Mark 1:41
segments: Jesus, moved with compassion, put out his hand and touched him, saying, "I do choose, be clean!"

entries.title: Mark 1:42
segments: The leprosy at once left him, and he was made clean.

entries.title: Mark 1:43
segments: Jesus immediately sent him away, charging him sternly and saying:

entries.title: Mark 1:44
segments: "See you say nothing to any one; but go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your purification what Moses commanded for a testimony to them."

entries.title: Mark 1:45
segments: But he went out and began to tell every one and to publish it broadcast, so that Jesus could no longer enter any town openly; but he had to remain outside in lonely places, and people kept coming to him from every quarter.
